svg.title: Framing, encoding, semantics - and the peer you did not upgrade
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch dividing a protocol into three separated bands labelled framing, encoding and semantics, each with the single question it answers; the same message drawn to scale as bars of 113.8 bytes of JSON, 81.1 bytes of MessagePack and 47.8 bytes of Protobuf with measured decode times of 4.44, 1.19 and 1.84 microseconds beneath; a compatibility panel where an old v1 client silently ignores a new currency field but a renamed field is crossed out in red; and a reconnect timeline with retries at one, two, four and eight seconds plus jitter, above a struck-through row of evenly spaced retries labelled thundering herd.
svg.text: Framing, encoding, semantics - and the peer you did not upgrade
who may say what, and when?
change to one forces a change
to the other two. That is how
the SAME message, drawn to scale
msgpack DECODES faster than protobuf in Python,
and is bigger on the wire. Measure both; do not
and gzip on a single 114-byte message makes it BIGGER: 115.9 B
the field that decides how long the protocol lives
v1 ignores the field it does not know. Nothing breaks.
a rename is a DELETE plus an ADD. v1 reads null and books nothing.
evenly spaced retries: every client comes back
at the same instant -> thundering herd
...and how do you know the peer is still there?
